doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Humor in jazz
summary: Ellis says humor is a great part of jazz and finds humorless playing sterile.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: How much is humor a part of the very fabric of jazz?

Oh, I think it’s a great part. And you can see a lot of players who don’t put any humor in it. And you can tell. It’s very sad. They play the notes but it’s dreary you know. Humor and melancholy is nice, and you know sometimes a little sadness, but humor is, oh boy, I don’t have any use for somebody who plays with no humor. It’s very sterile you know.
